title: Service-Recovery Courtesy Policy — Hospital Account (Encounter Billing)
content:
## 1. When a courtesy is owed, and when one may be granted

On a Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) account whose financial class was corrected to self-pay after its final bill and whose summary statements were issued while its coverage-terminated postings carried no uninsured discount, one service-recovery courtesy adjustment is owed for that failure whether or not the patient reports it. It is sourced to the account's most recent coverage-terminated posting by posting date (of two posted on the same day, the one recorded first), in the amount this rule fixes, never more than the patient class's service-recovery courtesy maximum and never more than the current patient balance.

On every other account a representative may grant one service-recovery courtesy adjustment when the patient reports a documented service failure (a billing error already corrected on the account, or a statement sent during an active billing hold), up to the courtesy maximum and never more than the current patient balance.

## 2. Where no courtesy is granted, and the prompt-pay discount

A courtesy adjustment is never granted on an account in bad-debt status or on a balance under an active payment plan. A courtesy owed under this rule does not take away the account's prompt-pay discount, while any other courtesy is not combined with a prompt-pay discount on the same account.

## 3. When the courtesy is fixed

On a self-pay account that carries coverage-terminated liability postings, the courtesy is not fixed until an uninsured discount stands against one of those postings.

On a self-pay account whose stay has ended and whose final bill has dropped, that carries observation-hour charge lines and that is not priced under a self-pay package, the courtesy is not fixed until an observation-rate discount stands against one of those lines.

## 4. Posting reference: `post_service_recovery_courtesy_69e36558`

**Capability.** Posts a service-recovery courtesy adjustment on one hospital account for a documented billing failure. One call books one adjustment of kind `SERVICE_RECOVERY_COURTESY` on the account, dated today and pointing back to the account record that documents the service failure, and lowers the account's patient balance by the amount given. The patient sees the courtesy on the account activity and a lower balance.

**Invocation.** An agent-side tool, unlocked by the representative and then called: `post_service_recovery_courtesy_69e36558`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `customer_id` | identifier: the patient reference number of the account holder, as returned by the patient profile lookup |
| `encounter_id` | identifier: the hospital account (HAR) number of the account receiving the courtesy, as returned by the hospital-account lookup for this patient |
| `source_txn_id` | identifier: the reference number of the account activity record that documents the service failure, as shown in that account's activity list |
| `amount` | the courtesy in USD, a positive amount with 2 decimal places, stored rounded half-up to the cent exactly as given |

**Return.** A confirmation string with the adjustment reference (the new activity reference number), the account, the source (the activity record named), the amount (USD, 2 decimal places), the posted date (today, YYYY-MM-DD) and the new balance (USD, 2 decimal places, after this courtesy). A returned adjustment reference means the courtesy is on the account.
